title: An element lifting (1,0) in a finite algebra is a root of a monic polynomial reducing to (x-1)x^d
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$, and $A\to B$ a finite ring map ($B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module). Suppose that $B/IB=B_1\times B_2$ is a product of $A/I$-algebras such that the structure map $A/I\to B_1$ is surjective, and let $b\in B$ be an element whose image in $B/IB$ is $(1,0)$. Then there are an integer $d\ge1$ and a monic polynomial $f\in A[x]$ with $f(b)=0$ in $B$ and $f\equiv(x-1)x^d$ modulo $I$; equivalently $f=x^d(x-1)+a_dx^d+\dots+a_1x+a_0$ with $a_0,\dots,a_d\in I$.
